claims.text: ADR 0012 serves every shop from one deployment and names two reopen conditions; the first: a shop whose contract demands its own copy gets a separate copy of the same system, other shops served as before; the product owner's earlier ask got 'no, until a contract demands it'.

ADR 0016: each shop may use at most a fixed share (assumed a quarter of 20) of the product reads a process serves at once; a read beyond the cap is refused; the cap is not reserved; not in code at stage-4: Program.cs keeps the orders and catalog-reads limits.

ADR 0033 (not built at stage-4): a plan is a set of numbers (share of concurrent reads under ADR 0016, number of staff accounts, chat on or off, data retention, assumed); a plan is a cap, not a reservation.

Challenge table: five rows; four answers name an ADR or a file, the fifth (shop with its own database under ADR 0026: drop it after the wait) applies the leaving deep dive; four rows have next step 'none' and no owner; the deletion row: record the deletion, Shop team.

Leaving: the shop moves to leaving and a job exports its data; after 30 days (assumed) rows are deleted in batches in donhang, donhang_payments, donhang_notifications and donhang_support; reporting totals are rebuilt (ADR 0031); Redis copies end by TTL; backup copies end when backups expire.
The last day a leaving shop's data exists is the deletion date plus the backup retention period.
Deletion runs in batches, not one large delete, so no lock is held long on shared tables serving other shops.

Risks table: backup retention making the final deletion date later than the shop expects is owned by the product owner with the legal department, next step: state it in the terms; a leaving shop with a pending refund is open, owned by the Ordering team: wait for the refund, then delete.

cluster-cost.md: every cluster runs its platform (Argo CD, Git server and others) whatever its traffic, and each added cluster or environment pays that part again; no lever reduces it except removing a cluster or environment.
claims.source_hint: docs/design/cluster-cost.md @ stage-4, Phần nền cố định mỗi cluster, Đòn bẩy

claims.text: ADR 0022 runs production on managed Kubernetes from one provider; its reopen conditions: a customer's contract demands own machines or data in a stated place; the provider's fee exceeds the assumed cost of running the cluster in-house (column A).
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0022-production-tren-kubernetes-managed.md @ stage-4, Quyết định and Điều kiện mở lại

claims.text: ADR 0012 consequence: one error or failed deploy reaches every shop at once; its rejected option of one copy per shop multiplies every deploy, migration, dashboard and alert.
claims.source_hint: docs/adr/0012-phuc-vu-moi-cua-hang-tu-mot-ban-trien-khai.md @ stage-4, Các phương án and Hệ quả

claims.text: A cluster of its own is right for a shop when a contract demands own machines or data in a stated place (ADR 0022's reopen condition); no such contract is recorded in Đơn Hàng's documents, so ADR 0022 stands and the shop stays on the shared cluster.
claims.source_hint: ADR 0022 @ stage-4 line 78; ADR 0012 @ stage-4 lines 61-63

claims.text: ADR 0033 revisit conditions: shops need free colours or a logo; sign-ups grow until the saga job is a bottleneck; a plan needs reserved capacity instead of a cap. The review's 'ADRs to write' plans a new ADR for free colours or a logo.
Risks table: mass fake sign-ups are owned by the Shop team; next step: limit sign-ups per email address and verify the email before step 2 (creating the first staff account).
data-ownership.md: shops rows and the plans table are owned by Ordering in donhang, run by the Shop team (assumed); Redis product copies expire by TTL; backups and WAL hold copies of every database.
Promising one paying customer its own deployment without a contract that demands it creates a second release schedule the team did not plan for.

data-ownership.md: four databases, one per service: donhang (Catalog and Ordering), donhang_payments (Payments), donhang_notifications (Notifications), donhang_support (Support, chat); the reporting database holds per-shop daily totals copied from Ordering and Payments (ADR 0031, not at stage-4).
The leaving deep dive's 30-day wait (assumed) runs from the shop moving to leaving until its rows are deleted; the lesson calls it the grace period.

beyond_scope: Fifth challenge row (shop with its own database) and the risks rows (pending refund, backup retention, fake sign-ups) read from the quoted review; no decision reopened.
Legal department named only as owner of a risk row; no data-deletion regulation taught (depth_notes).
